title.zh: 卷38 列傳第3 劉昉 鄭譯 柳裘 皇甫績 盧賁
title.en: Volume 38 Biographies 3: Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, Liu Qiu, Huang Fuji, Lu Ben
title.raw: 卷38 列傳第3 劉昉 鄭譯 柳裘 皇甫績 盧賁 Volume 38 Biographies 3: Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, Liu Qiu, Huang Fuji, Lu Ben

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 劉昉劉昉，博陵望都人也。

translations.literal: Liu Fang, Liu Fang, was a native of Wangdu in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang was a native of Wangdu in Boling commandery.

sentences.zh: 父孟良，大司農。

translations.literal: His father Mengliang was Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mengliang had served as Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 從魏武入關，周太祖以為東梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wu of Wei in entering the Pass, and the Zhou founder appointed him Eastern Liangzhou governor.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Wu of Wei into the pass, he was made Eastern Liangzhou governor by the Zhou founder Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 昉性輕狡，有奸數。

translations.literal: Fang by nature was frivolous and cunning, possessed of treacherous schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was frivolous and slippery by nature, always ready with some underhand scheme.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，以功臣子入侍皇太子。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, as son of a meritorious minister he entered to attend the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, he entered palace service to attend the crown prince as the son of a meritorious minister.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝嗣位，以技佞見狎，出入宮掖，寵冠一時。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, through skill and flattery he was treated familiarly, coming and going in the inner palace, his favor surpassing all in that time.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, his talents and sycophancy won intimate favor; he moved freely through the inner palace and for a time enjoyed unrivaled favor.

sentences.zh: 授大都督，遷小禦正，與禦正中大夫顏之儀並見親信。

translations.literal: He was appointed Great Commander, promoted to Junior Director of the Imperial Carriage, and together with Senior Director of the Imperial Carriage Yan Zhiyi was alike treated with close trust.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand commander, then promoted to junior director of the imperial carriage, and he and senior director Yan Zhiyi alike enjoyed the emperor's close trust.

sentences.zh: 及帝不悆，召方及之儀俱入臥內，屬以後事。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, Fang and Zhiyi were both summoned into the bedchamber and charged with affairs to come.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor grew gravely ill, Fang and Zhiyi were both called to his bedside and entrusted with what was to follow.

sentences.zh: 帝喑不復能言。

translations.literal: The emperor was mute and could no longer speak.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had lost speech entirely.

sentences.zh: 昉見靜帝幼沖，不堪負荷。

translations.literal: Fang saw that Emperor Jing was young and tender, unable to bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Fang saw that Emperor Jing was a mere child, unfit to bear the burden of rule.

sentences.zh: 然昉素知高祖，又以後父之故，有重名於天下，遂與鄭譯謀，引高祖輔政。

translations.literal: Yet Fang had long known Yang Jian, and because of his position as the empress's father he had great renown in the realm; he therefore plotted with Zheng Yi to bring in Yang Jian to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had long known Yang Jian, who because he was the empress dowager's father enjoyed great renown throughout the realm; he therefore plotted with Zheng Yi to bring Yang Jian in as regent.

sentences.zh: 高祖固讓，不敢當。

translations.literal: Yang Jian firmly declined, not daring to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian repeatedly declined, saying he dared not take the role.

sentences.zh: 昉曰：「公若為，當速為之；

translations.literal: Fang said, "If you, sir, will act, you should act quickly;
translations.idiomatic: Fang said, "If you mean to act, sir, act at once;

sentences.zh: 如不為，昉自為也。

translations.literal: if you will not act, Fang will act himself."
translations.idiomatic: if you will not, I shall act in your stead."

sentences.zh: 」高祖乃從之。

translations.literal: Yang Jian then followed him.
translations.idiomatic: At that Yang Jian yielded and accepted.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為承相，以昉為司馬。

translations.literal: When Yang Jian became chancellor, he appointed Fang as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Jian became chancellor, he made Fang his marshal.

sentences.zh: 時宣帝弟漢王贊居禁中，每與高祖同帳而坐。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan's younger brother, Prince Han Zan, dwelt in the inner palace and each day sat in the same tent with Yang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Xuan's younger brother, Prince Han of Han, lived in the inner palace and daily shared a tent with Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 昉飾美妓進於贊，贊甚悅之。

translations.literal: Fang dressed beautiful courtesans and presented them to Zan; Zan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fang sent in beautifully adorned courtesans to please Zan, who took to them eagerly.

sentences.zh: 昉因說贊曰：「大王先帝之弟，時望所歸。

translations.literal: Fang thereupon urged Zan, saying, "Your Highness is the late emperor's younger brother, toward whom the hopes of the age turn.
translations.idiomatic: Fang then urged Zan, saying, "Your Highness is the late emperor's own brother, the man to whom all eyes turn.

sentences.zh: 孺子幼沖，豈堪大事！

translations.literal: The child is young and tender—how can he bear great affairs!
translations.idiomatic: That boy on the throne is still a child—how could he bear the weight of empire!

sentences.zh: 今先帝初崩，群情尚擾，王且歸第。

translations.literal: Now that the late emperor has just died and popular feeling is still unsettled, Your Highness should for the present return to your residence.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor has only just died and the realm is still unsettled; for now you should withdraw to your own residence.

sentences.zh: 待事寧之後，入為天子，此萬全之計也。

translations.literal: When affairs have settled, enter and become Son of Heaven—this is a plan of complete security."
translations.idiomatic: When things have quieted, you can enter the palace and take the throne yourself—a plan without risk."

sentences.zh: 」贊時年未弱冠，性識庸下，聞昉之說，以為信然，遂從之。

translations.literal: Zan was then not yet twenty, his nature and understanding coarse and low; hearing Fang's words, he took them as true and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was not yet twenty, dull of mind and shallow in judgment; he believed Fang's counsel and did as he was told.

sentences.zh: 高祖以昉有定策之功，拜下大將軍，封黃國公，與沛國公鄭譯皆為心膂。

translations.literal: Yang Jian, because Fang had the merit of settling the policy, appointed him junior grand general, enfeoffed him as duke of Huang state, and together with Duke of Pei Zheng Yi made him a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fang had helped settle the succession, Yang Jian made him junior grand general and enfeoffed him as Duke of Huang; he and Duke of Pei Zheng Yi became Yang Jian's closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 前後賞賜巨萬，出入以甲士自衛，朝野傾矚，稱為黃、沛。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after amounted to tens of thousands; going out and coming in he was guarded by armored soldiers; court and countryside looked to him with admiration, calling them Huang and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards in the tens of thousands flowed to them; armored guards attended their comings and goings; all eyes in court and country were on them, and people spoke of "Huang and Pei."

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「劉昉牽前，鄭譯推後。

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: "Liu Fang pulls in front, Zheng Yi pushes from behind."
translations.idiomatic: A saying of the day ran: "Liu Fang pulls from the fore, Zheng Yi pushes from behind."

sentences.zh: 」昉自恃其功，頗有驕色。

translations.literal: Fang relied on his merit and showed considerable arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, trusting in his merit, grew visibly arrogant.

sentences.zh: 然性粗疏，溺於財利，富商大賈，朝夕盈門。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was coarse and careless; he drowned himself in wealth and profit, and great merchants morning and evening filled his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was coarse and careless by nature, obsessed with profit; wealthy merchants thronged his gate from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 于時尉迥起兵，高祖令韋孝寬討之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuchi Jiong raised troops; Yang Jian ordered Wei Xiaokuan to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion, and Yang Jian sent Wei Xiaokuan to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 至武陟，諸將不一。

translations.literal: When they reached Wuzhi, the generals were not of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuzhi the commanders could not agree on a course of action.

sentences.zh: 高祖欲遣昉、譯一人往監軍，因謂之曰：「須得心膂以統大軍，公等兩人，誰當行者？

translations.literal: Yang Jian wished to send either Fang or Yi to oversee the army, and therefore said to them, "I need a trusted confidant to command the great army—you two, which of you should go?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian meant to send either Fang or Yi to supervise the campaign and asked them, "I need a man I can trust at the head of this army—which of you two will go?"

sentences.zh: 」昉自言未嘗為將，譯又以母老為請，高祖不怪。

translations.literal: Fang said himself that he had never been a general; Yi also pleaded an aged mother; Yang Jian did not blame them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang pleaded that he had never commanded troops; Yi cited an aged mother; Yang Jian did not reproach them.

sentences.zh: 而高熲請行，遂遣之。

translations.literal: But Gao Jiong requested to go, and he was therefore sent.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong volunteered, and Yang Jian sent him instead.

sentences.zh: 由是恩禮漸薄。

translations.literal: From this their favor and courtesy gradually grew thin.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Yang Jian's favor toward them steadily cooled.

sentences.zh: 又王謙、司馬消難相繼而反，高祖憂之，忘寢與食。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Qian and Sima Xiaonan rose in rebellion one after another; Yang Jian was anxious over this and forgot sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian and Sima Xiaonan then rebelled in turn; Yang Jian was so troubled that he scarcely ate or slept.

sentences.zh: 昉逸遊縱酒，不以職司為意，相府事物，多所遺落。

translations.literal: Fang wandered in idleness and drank to excess, not taking his office to heart; affairs of the chancellor's bureau were in many cases neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Fang idled and drank, caring nothing for his duties, and much business at the chancellor's office went unattended.

sentences.zh: 高祖深銜之，以高熲代為司馬。

translations.literal: Yang Jian deeply resented this and replaced him with Gao Jiong as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian deeply resented this and replaced him as marshal with Gao Jiong.

sentences.zh: 是後益見疏忌。

translations.literal: After this he was increasingly seen with distance and suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he was increasingly kept at a distance and viewed with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，進位柱國，改封舒國公，閒居無事，不復任使。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he was advanced to pillar of state, changed enfeoffment to duke of Shu state, lived at leisure without duties, and was no longer employed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Fang was promoted to pillar of state and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shu, but was left idle and given no further appointments.

sentences.zh: 昉自以佐命元功，中被疏遠，甚不自安。

translations.literal: Fang considered himself a founding minister of the first merit, yet midway was kept at a distance; he was very ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, who had counted himself among the founders of the dynasty, found himself cast aside and grew deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 後遇京師饑，上令禁酒，昉使妾賃屋，當壚沽酒。

translations.literal: Later, when the capital suffered famine, the emperor ordered a ban on wine; Fang had a concubine rent a house and sell wine at the counter.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when famine struck the capital, the emperor banned the sale of wine; Fang had a concubine rent a shopfront and sell wine over the counter.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史梁毗劾奏昉曰：「臣聞處貴則戒之以奢，持滿則守之以約。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Attendant Censor Liang Pi impeached Fang, saying, "Your servant has heard that in occupying high rank one is warned against extravagance, and in holding fullness one is kept to restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary attendant censor Liang Pi memorialized against Fang, saying, "I have heard that high rank should be guarded with warnings against extravagance, and that fullness should be held in check by restraint.

sentences.zh: 昉既位列群公，秩高庶尹，縻爵稍久，厚祿已淹，正當戒滿歸盈，鑒斯止足，何乃規曲蘖之潤，競錐刀之末，身昵酒徒，家為逋藪？

translations.literal: Fang already stands among the nobles, his rank higher than many ministers; he has long enjoyed enfeoffment and his generous salary has long flowed—he should rightly guard against fullness and return from excess, take this mirror of knowing when to stop, yet why does he scheme for the profit of yeast and mash, compete for the tip of the awl's blade, keep company with drunkards, and make his house a den of debt?
translations.idiomatic: Fang already ranks among the highest nobles, his stipend long and heavy; he ought to know when he has enough and hold back from excess—yet why does he chase petty profits from brewing, haggle over trifles, consort with drunkards, and turn his household into a refuge for debtors?

sentences.zh: 若不糾繩，何以肅厲！

translations.literal: If he is not disciplined, how can order and sternness be upheld!"
translations.idiomatic: If such conduct is not punished, how can discipline be maintained!"

sentences.zh: 」有詔不治。

translations.literal: An edict was issued that he was not to be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the matter not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 昉鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Fang was depressed and could not realize his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Fang brooded, his ambitions thwarted.

sentences.zh: 時柱國梁士彥、宇文忻俱失職忿望，昉並與之交，數相來往。

translations.literal: At that time the pillars of state Liang Shiyan and Yuwen Xin both had lost office and nursed resentment; Fang associated with them both and frequently visited back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: The pillars of state Liang Shiyan and Yuwen Xin had both lost their posts and nursed grievances; Fang befriended them and they met often.

sentences.zh: 士彥妻有美色，昉因與私通，士彥不之知也，情好彌協，遂相與謀反，許推士彥為帝。

translations.literal: Shiyan's wife was beautiful; Fang therefore had a secret liaison with her, and Shiyan did not know it; their friendship grew ever closer, and they thereupon plotted rebellion together, agreeing to set up Shiyan as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan's wife was beautiful; Fang took her as his lover while Shiyan knew nothing of it. Their intimacy deepened until they plotted rebellion together, agreeing to make Shiyan emperor.

sentences.zh: 後事泄，上窮治之。

translations.literal: Later the affair leaked out, and the emperor prosecuted it to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot came to light, the emperor investigated it thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 昉自知不免，默無所對。

translations.literal: Fang knew he could not escape and was silent, answering nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Fang knew he could not escape and said nothing in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 下詔誅之，曰：

translations.literal: An edict was issued to execute them, saying:
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned them to death, reading:

sentences.zh: 朕君臨四海，慈愛為心。

translations.literal: We rule the four seas, with compassion as our heart.
translations.idiomatic: We rule the four seas, and compassion is our guiding principle.

sentences.zh: 加以起自布衣，入升皇極，公卿之內，非親則友，位雖差等，情皆舊人。

translations.literal: Moreover, rising from common cloth to ascending the imperial pinnacle, among the nobles none are not kin or friends; though ranks differ in degree, in feeling all are old companions.
translations.idiomatic: Having risen from humble origins to the throne, we count among the nobles none who are not kin or old companions; though rank may differ, the bond is that of long friendship.

sentences.zh: 護短全長，恆思覆育，每殷勤戒約，言無不盡。

translations.literal: We shield faults and preserve strengths, ever thinking to shelter and nurture; at every turn we earnestly admonish and bind with covenant, our words never incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: We have shielded your faults and cherished your strengths, ever seeking to shelter and nurture you, admonishing you earnestly time and again, holding nothing back.

sentences.zh: 天之歷數，定於杳冥，豈慮苞藏之心，能為國家之害？

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate is fixed in the dark unseen—did We ever suppose that hearts harboring treachery could become harm to the state?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate rests in what none can foresee—did we ever imagine that treacherous hearts concealed among us could bring harm to the state?

sentences.zh: 欲使其長守富貴，不觸刑書故也。

translations.literal: We wished to make them long keep wealth and honor and not touch the penal code—that is why.
translations.idiomatic: We wished only that you might long enjoy wealth and honor without ever falling under the penal code.

sentences.zh: 上柱國、郕國公梁士彥，上柱國、國公宇文忻，柱國、舒國公劉昉等，朕受命之初，並展勤力，酬勳報效，榮高祿重。

translations.literal: Senior pillar of state, Duke of Bi Liang Shiyan; senior pillar of state, state duke Yuwen Xin; pillar of state, Duke of Shu Liu Fang and others—in the beginning of Our receiving the mandate all displayed diligent effort, were rewarded for merit and repaid for service, with glory high and salary heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Senior pillar of state and Duke of Bi, Liang Shiyan; senior pillar of state and state duke, Yuwen Xin; pillar of state and Duke of Shu, Liu Fang, and others—all at the beginning of our reign showed loyal service and were rewarded with the highest honors and richest stipends.

sentences.zh: 待之既厚，愛之實隆，朝夕宴言，備知朕意。

translations.literal: We treated them already with great generosity and loved them in truth with deep elevation; morning and evening at feast and talk, they fully knew Our mind.
translations.idiomatic: We treated them generously and held them in genuine affection; day after day we spoke with them at leisure, and they knew our mind completely.

sentences.zh: 但心如溪壑，志等豺狼，不荷朝恩，忽謀逆亂。

translations.literal: Yet their hearts were like streams and ravines, their wills equal to wolves and jackals; they did not bear the court's grace and suddenly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their hearts were bottomless as ravines, their wills wolfish; ungrateful for the court's grace, they suddenly plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 士彥爰始幼來，恆自誣罔，稱有相者，雲其應籙，年過六十，必據九五。

translations.literal: Shiyan from his earliest youth onward constantly deceived himself, saying there was a physiognomist who declared he matched the tally, and that past sixty he would surely occupy the Nine-Five.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth Shiyan had deluded himself with fortune-tellers who told him he was destined for the throne and that once past sixty he would surely rule as Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 初平尉迥，暫臨相州，已有反心，彰于行路。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong was first pacified, he was temporarily posted to Xiangzhou and already had a rebellious heart, manifest on the public roads.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong's rebellion was first suppressed, Shiyan was briefly posted to Xiangzhou; his rebellious intent was already plain to all who passed along the roads.

sentences.zh: 朕即遣人代之，不聲其罪。

translations.literal: We immediately sent someone to replace him, not proclaiming his crime.
translations.idiomatic: We at once sent another to replace him, without publicly announcing his offense.

sentences.zh: 入京之後，逆意轉深。

translations.literal: After entering the capital, his rebellious intent turned deeper.
translations.idiomatic: After he came to the capital, his rebellious intent only deepened.

sentences.zh: 忻、昉之徒，言相扶助。

translations.literal: Xin, Fang, and their sort spoke of mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, Fang, and their circle spoke of aiding one another.

sentences.zh: 士彥許率僮僕，克期不遠，欲于蒲州起事，即斷河橋，捉黎陽之關，塞河陽之路，劫調布以為牟甲，募盜賊而為戰士，就食之人，亦雲易集。

translations.literal: Shiyan promised to lead servants and retainers, the set day not far off; he wished to raise the affair at Puzhou, immediately cut the river bridge, seize the pass of Liyang, block the road of Heyang, plunder tax cloth to make armor, recruit bandits as fighting men, and even men coming for food, he said, would be easy to gather.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan promised to lead his household retainers on a day not far off: he would rise at Puzhou, cut the Yellow River bridge, seize the Liyang pass, block the Heyang road, seize tax cloth for armor, enlist bandits as soldiers, and even hungry men, he said, would be easy to rally.

sentences.zh: 輕忽朝廷，嗤笑官人，自謂一朝奮發，無人當者。

translations.literal: He slighted the court, mocked officials, and declared that if he roused himself in a morning, none could stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: He despised the court, mocked its officers, and boasted that once he roused himself, none could stand in his way.

sentences.zh: 其第二子剛，每常苦諫，第三子叔諧，固深勸獎。

translations.literal: His second son Gang constantly remonstrated in bitter earnest; his third son Shuxie firmly urged and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Gang repeatedly urged him to desist; his third son Shuxie strongly encouraged the plot.

sentences.zh: 朕既聞知，猶恐枉濫，乃授晉部之任，欲驗蒲州之情。

translations.literal: When We had heard and knew, We still feared wrongful excess and therefore gave him the post of Jin region, wishing to test his feelings toward Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When we learned of this, we still feared acting unjustly and therefore appointed him to the Jin region, intending to test his intentions regarding Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 士彥得以欣然，雲是天贊，忻及昉等，皆賀時來。

translations.literal: Shiyan was thereby pleased and said it was Heaven's support; Xin, Fang, and the rest all congratulated him that the time had come.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan rejoiced, calling it Heaven's blessing; Xin, Fang, and the others all congratulated him that their hour had come.

sentences.zh: 忻往定鄴城，自矜不已，位極人臣，猶恨賞薄。

translations.literal: Xin went to pacify Ye city and was unceasingly self-congratulatory; his rank reached the utmost among subjects, yet he still resented thin reward.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin pacified Ye, he never ceased to boast of his achievement; though he stood at the summit of subjecthood, he still complained his rewards were meager.

sentences.zh: 雲我欲反，何慮不成。

translations.literal: He said, "If I wish to rebel, why worry that it will not succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "If I choose to rebel, what is there to fear of failure?"

sentences.zh: 怒色忿言，所在流布。

translations.literal: Angry looks and resentful words spread everywhere he went.
translations.idiomatic: His angry words and resentful talk spread wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 朕深念其功，不計其禮，任以武候，授以領軍，寄之爪牙，委之心腹。

translations.literal: We deeply recalled his merit and did not reckon his discourtesy, appointing him to the Martial Guard, granting him command of the palace guard, entrusting him as Our claws and teeth, committing him as Our heart's core.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his past merit, we overlooked his discourtesy, made him commander of the martial guard, gave him command of the palace armies, and trusted him as our own right hand.

sentences.zh: 忻密為異計，樹党宮闈，多奏親友，入參宿衛。

translations.literal: Xin secretly made a separate plan, planted a faction in the inner palace, repeatedly memorialized for kin and friends to enter and join the night guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xin secretly laid other plans, built a faction within the palace, and repeatedly had kinsmen and friends appointed to the night guard.

sentences.zh: 朕推心待物，言刻依許。

translations.literal: We treated things with open heart and at every word carved our assent.
translations.idiomatic: We met him with open trust and granted his every request.

sentences.zh: 為而弗止，心跡漸彰，仍解禁兵，令其改悔。

translations.literal: He acted and would not stop; heart and tracks gradually showed clear; We still removed his command of troops, wishing him to reform and repent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he would not cease; his intent grew ever plainer, and we even stripped him of military command, hoping he would repent.

sentences.zh: 而志規不逞，愈結於懷，乃與士彥情意偏厚，要請神明，誓不負約。

translations.literal: Yet his will and scheme did not succeed and bound ever tighter in his breast; he then with Shiyan had feelings especially thick, invoked the spirits, and swore not to break covenant.
translations.idiomatic: His ambitions only hardened; he grew especially close to Shiyan, invoked the spirits, and swore never to break faith with him.

sentences.zh: 俱營賊逆，逢則交謀，委彥河東，自許關右，蒲津之事，即望從征，兩軍結東西之旅，一舉合連橫之勢，然後北破晉陽，還圖宗社。

translations.literal: Together they plotted treacherous rebellion; when they met they exchanged counsel—entrusting Shiyan with Hedong, Xin promising himself the land west of the Pass; on the affair at Pujin he at once hoped to follow the campaign; two armies would join east and west hosts, one stroke combining the power of horizontal alliance, then north to break Jinyang and return to scheme for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Together they plotted treason, conferring whenever they met: Shiyan was to hold Hedong, Xin the land west of the Pass; at the crossing at Pujin they would join forces; east and west armies would unite in one stroke, then march north to take Jinyang and turn back to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 昉入佐相府，便為非法，三度事發，二度其婦自論。

translations.literal: When Fang entered to assist the chancellor's bureau, he at once acted unlawfully; three times matters broke out, twice his wife came forward in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fang entered the chancellor's office he broke the law repeatedly; three times his offenses came to light, and twice his wife pleaded his case before the court.

sentences.zh: 常雲姓是「卯金刀」，名是「一萬日」，劉氏應王，為萬日天子。

translations.literal: He constantly said his surname was "mao-jin-dao" and his given name was "ten thousand days"—the Liu clan should be king and become the ten-thousand-day Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He often said that the character Liu split into "mao, metal, knife" and that his name meant "ten thousand days"—proof that the house of Liu was destined to rule for ten thousand days as Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 朕訓之導之，示其利害，每加寬宥，望其修改。

translations.literal: We instructed and guided him, showed him benefit and harm, repeatedly extended leniency, hoping he would reform.
translations.idiomatic: We admonished and guided him, showed him what he stood to gain or lose, and repeatedly pardoned him, hoping he would mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 口請自新，志存如舊，亦與士彥情好深重，逆節奸心，盡探肝鬲。

translations.literal: With his mouth he asked to renew himself, but his will remained as before; he also with Shiyan had deep affection, and their rebellious conduct and treacherous hearts were fully probed to the liver and diaphragm.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of reform while his heart remained unchanged; he too was deeply bound to Shiyan, and their treasonous intent was laid bare in every detail.

sentences.zh: 嘗共士彥論太白所犯，問東井之間，思秦地之亂，訪軒轅之裡，願宮掖之災。

translations.literal: He once with Shiyan discussed the zone violated by Tai Bai, inquired into the space between the Eastern Well, thought on disorder in Qin territory, sought the quarter of Xuanyuan, and wished for calamity in the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shiyan once discussed the movements of the planet Venus, asking what turmoil in Qin lands and disaster in the palace quarters the stars foretold.

sentences.zh: 唯待蒲阪事興，欲在關內應接。

translations.literal: He only waited for the affair at Puban to rise, wishing to respond within the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He waited only for the rising at Puban so that he might respond from within the Pass.

sentences.zh: 殘賊之策，千端萬緒。

translations.literal: Their brutal rebel stratagems had a thousand beginnings and ten thousand threads.
translations.idiomatic: Their treacherous schemes branched in a thousand directions.

sentences.zh: 惟忻及昉，名位並高，寧肯北面曲躬，臣於士彥，乃是各懷不遜，圖成亂階，一得擾攘之基，方逞吞併之事。

translations.literal: Only Xin and Fang—with name and rank both high—would they truly bow north and bend the body to serve Shiyan as subjects? Rather each harbored insubordination, scheming to complete the ladder of disorder; once they gained a foundation of turmoil, then they would display the business of swallowing and annexing.
translations.idiomatic: As for Xin and Fang, men of the highest rank and station—would they truly bow and serve Shiyan as his subjects? Each nursed his own ambition, seeking only to sow chaos so that, once turmoil began, he might seize power for himself.

sentences.zh: 人之奸詐，一至於此！

translations.literal: Human treachery and deceit—to this degree!
translations.idiomatic: That human treachery could reach such a pitch!

sentences.zh: 雖國有常刑，罪在不赦，朕載思草創，鹹著厥誠，情用湣然，未忍極法。

translations.literal: Although the state has constant punishments and their crimes were among those not pardoned, We constantly recalled the founding and all had shown their sincerity; Our feeling was moved to pity and We could not bear the utmost law.
translations.idiomatic: Though the law calls for death and their crimes are unpardonable, we remembered how they had served at the founding of the dynasty and could not bring ourselves to apply the harshest penalty to all.

sentences.zh: 士彥、忻、昉，身為謀首，叔諧贊成父意，義實難容，並已處盡。

translations.literal: Shiyan, Xin, and Fang, their persons the chiefs of the plot; Shuxie who supported his father's intent—the principle truly hard to tolerate—all have been disposed of to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan, Xin, and Fang, the ringleaders, and Shuxie, who urged his father on—none could be spared—and all have been executed.

sentences.zh: 士彥、忻、昉兄弟叔侄，特恕其命，有官者除名。

translations.literal: The brothers, uncles, and nephews of Shiyan, Xin, and Fang are specially spared their lives; those who held office are removed from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers, uncles, and nephews of Shiyan, Xin, and Fang are specially spared; those who held office are struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 士彥小男女、忻母妻女及小男並放。

translations.literal: Shiyan's young sons and daughters, Xin's mother, wife, daughters, and young sons are all released.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan's young children, Xin's mother, wife, daughters, and young sons are all released.

sentences.zh: 士彥、叔諧妻妾及資財田宅，忻、昉妻妾及資財田宅，悉沒官。

translations.literal: The wives and concubines of Shiyan and Shuxie and their property, fields, and houses; the wives and concubines of Xin and Fang and their property, fields, and houses—all are confiscated to the state.
translations.idiomatic: The wives and concubines of Shiyan and Shuxie, with all their property, fields, and houses, and those of Xin and Fang, are all confiscated by the state.

sentences.zh: 士彥、昉兒年十五以上遠配。

translations.literal: Shiyan's and Fang's sons fifteen years and above are banished to distant assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Shiyan and Fang aged fifteen or above are banished to distant posts.

sentences.zh: 上儀同薛摩兒，是士彥交舊，上柱國府戶曹參軍事裴石達，是士彥府僚，反狀逆心，巨細皆委。

translations.literal: Senior attendant of the first rank Xue Mo'er was Shiyan's old associate; senior pillar of state's bureau household registrar Pei Shida was Shiyan's bureau subordinate—the form of rebellion and treacherous heart, great and small, were all entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: Senior attendant of the first rank Xue Mo'er was Shiyan's old friend; registrar Pei Shida of the senior pillar's bureau was Shiyan's subordinate—they were entrusted with every detail of the plot.

sentences.zh: 薛摩兒聞語，仍相應和，俱不申陳，宜從大辟。

translations.literal: Xue Mo'er heard the words and still responded in accord; both did not report upward—they should follow capital execution.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Mo'er heard the plot and assented; neither reported it—both deserve death.

sentences.zh: 問即承引，頗是恕心，可除名免死。

translations.literal: When questioned they at once confessed and led the way; this shows a heart somewhat inclined to pardon—they may be removed from the registers and spared death.
translations.idiomatic: They confessed when questioned, showing some disposition to repent; they may be struck from the rolls and spared.

sentences.zh: 朕握圖當籙，六載於斯，政事徒勤，淳化未洽，興言軫念，良深歎憤！

translations.literal: We hold the chart and bear the tally; six years have passed here; in government affairs We are only diligent, yet pure transformation is not yet harmonized; raising words We bend Our thought—truly deep sighing and indignation!
translations.idiomatic: Six years have passed since we took the throne; though we labor at government, honest custom has not yet prevailed throughout the realm—and at this we sigh with deep grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，至朝堂，宇文忻見高熲，向之叩頭求哀。

translations.literal: Facing execution, when they came to the court hall, Yuwen Xin saw Gao Jiong and bowed his head to him begging for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: At the place of execution, as they were brought to the court hall, Yuwen Xin saw Gao Jiong and kowtowed to him, begging for his life.

sentences.zh: 昉勃然謂忻曰：「事形如此，何叩頭之有！

translations.literal: Fang angrily said to Xin, "Matters have taken this shape—what is there in bowing the head!"
translations.idiomatic: Fang flushed with anger and said to Xin, "Matters stand as they do—what use is there in kowtowing!"

sentences.zh: 」於是伏誅，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were executed by the sword, and their households were registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: They were then executed, and their families and property were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 後數日，上素服臨射殿，盡取昉敢、忻、士彥三家資物置於前，令百僚射取之，以為鑒誡雲。

translations.literal: Several days later, the emperor in plain dress came to the Archery Hall, took all the goods and property of the three houses of Fang, Xin, and Shiyan and placed them before him, ordered the hundred officials to shoot and take them, making it a warning lesson.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the emperor came to the Archery Hall in mourning dress, had all the confiscated goods of the Fang, Xin, and Shiyan households set out before the court, and ordered the officials to shoot at them and take what they hit, as a lesson to all.

sentences.zh: 鄭譯鄭譯，字正義，滎陽開封人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Yi, Zheng Yi, styled Zhengyi, was a native of Kaifeng in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi, whose style name was Zhengyi, was a native of Kaifeng in Xingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖瓊，魏太常。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiong was Wei Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiong had served as Wei Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 父道邕，魏司空。

translations.literal: His father Daoyong was Wei Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoyong had served as Wei Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 譯頗有學識，兼知鐘律，善騎射。

translations.literal: Yi had considerable learning, and also knew bells and pitch pipes; he was skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was well educated and versed in music theory; he was also skilled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 譯從祖開府文寬，尚魏平陽公主，則周太祖元後之妹也。

translations.literal: Yi's paternal uncle by descent, Defender-in-Chief Wen Kuan, married Princess Pingyang of Wei, who was a younger sister of the Zhou founder's primary consort.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's grand-uncle Wen Kuan, a defender-in-chief, had married Princess Pingyang of Wei, younger sister of the Zhou founder's principal consort.

sentences.zh: 主無子，太祖令譯後之。

translations.literal: The princess had no son; the Zhou founder ordered Yi to succeed to the line.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had no son, and the Zhou founder had Yi succeed to the household.

sentences.zh: 由是譯少為太祖所親，恆令與諸子遊集。

translations.literal: From this Yi in youth was treated with intimacy by the founder, who constantly had him gather and play with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Yi was treated as one of the founder's own sons and was constantly set to play with Yuwen Tai's boys.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，嘗詣相府司錄李長宗，長宗於眾中戲之。

translations.literal: When he was just over ten, he once called on the chancellor's bureau registrar Li Changzong; Changzong jested with him before the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: When he was barely in his teens he once visited the chancellor's registrar Li Changzong, who teased him before a crowd.

sentences.zh: 譯斂容謂長宗曰：「明公位望不輕，瞻仰斯屬，輒相玩狎，無乃喪德也。

translations.literal: Yi composed his bearing and said to Changzong, "Your Excellency's position and renown are not light; those who look up to such as you should not be treated with careless play—would this not be a loss of virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi composed himself and said, "Your Excellency's rank and reputation are weighty; those who look up to you ought not to be treated so lightly—would that not be a lapse of virtue?"

sentences.zh: 」長宗甚異之。

translations.literal: Changzong was greatly struck by this.
translations.idiomatic: Changzong was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 文寬後誕二子，譯複歸本生。

translations.literal: Wen Kuan later bore two sons, and Yi returned to his birth father.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Kuan later had two sons of his own, Yi returned to his birth family.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，起家給事中士，拜銀青光祿大夫，轉左侍上士。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou he first entered service as attendant gentleman, was appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace, and transferred to left attendant senior gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou he entered service as an attendant gentleman, was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace, and then promoted to left attendant senior gentleman.

sentences.zh: 與儀同劉昉恆侍帝側。

translations.literal: Together with attendant of the first rank Liu Fang he constantly attended at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: He and Liu Fang, an attendant of the first rank, constantly attended the emperor.

sentences.zh: 譯時喪妻，帝命譯尚梁安固公主。

translations.literal: Yi at that time had lost his wife; the emperor ordered Yi to marry Princess Angu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was widowed, the emperor had him marry Princess Angu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 及帝親總萬機，以為禦正下大夫，俄轉太子宮尹。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally took charge of all affairs, he was made junior director of the imperial carriage, and soon transferred to palace steward of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took personal charge of government, Yi was made junior director of the imperial carriage and soon became palace steward to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時太子多失德，內史中大夫烏丸軌每勸帝廢太子而立秦王，由是太子恆不自安。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince had many moral failings; inner secretary senior grand master Wuyan Gui constantly urged the emperor to depose the crown prince and establish the Prince of Qin, and from this the crown prince was ever ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had fallen into many faults; inner secretary Wuyan Gui repeatedly urged the emperor to depose him and make the Prince of Qin heir instead, and the crown prince lived in constant anxiety.

sentences.zh: 其後詔太子西征吐谷渾，太子乃陰謂譯曰：「秦王，上愛子也。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered the crown prince to campaign west against Tuyuhun; the crown prince secretly said to Yi, "The Prince of Qin is the emperor's beloved son.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the crown prince was ordered west against Tuyuhun, he confided to Yi, "The Prince of Qin is the emperor's favorite son.

sentences.zh: 烏丸軌，上信臣也。

translations.literal: Wuyan Gui is a trusted minister of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Gui enjoys the emperor's full trust.

sentences.zh: 今吾此行，得無扶蘇之事乎？

translations.literal: On this journey of mine, will there not be something like the affair of Fusu?"
translations.idiomatic: On this campaign of mine, am I not walking into another Fusu affair?"

sentences.zh: 」譯曰：「願殿下勉著仁孝，無失子道而已。

translations.literal: Yi said, "I wish Your Highness would strive to display benevolence and filial piety and not fail in the way of a son—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "Your Highness need only strive in benevolence and filial piety and keep to the way of a son.

sentences.zh: 勿為他慮。

translations.literal: Do not make other worries."
translations.idiomatic: Give no thought to other fears."

sentences.zh: 」太子然之。

translations.literal: The crown prince assented to this.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took comfort in this.

sentences.zh: 既破賊，譯以功最，賜爵開國子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: After the rebels were broken, Yi for the foremost merit was granted the title founding viscount with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy was defeated, Yi received the highest credit and was enfeoffed as founding viscount with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後坐褻狎皇太子，帝大怒，除名為民。

translations.literal: Later, on a charge of indecent familiarity with the crown prince, the emperor was greatly angered and struck his name from the registers, reducing him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was charged with indecent familiarity toward the crown prince; the emperor was furious and struck him from the rolls, reducing him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 太子複召之，譯戲狎如初。

translations.literal: The crown prince summoned him again, and Yi sported and treated him familiarly as before.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince summoned him back, and Yi resumed his familiar, playful ways as before.

sentences.zh: 因言于太子曰：「殿下何時可得據天下？

translations.literal: He then said to the crown prince, "When will Your Highness be able to hold all under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked the crown prince, "When will Your Highness take possession of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 」太子悅而益昵之。

translations.literal: The crown prince was pleased and grew even more intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was delighted and drew even closer to him.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，太子嗣位，是為宣帝。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, the crown prince succeeded—this is Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died the crown prince succeeded him as Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 超拜開府、內史下大夫、封歸昌縣公，邑一千戶，委以朝政。

translations.literal: He was promoted in one step to defender-in-chief and junior inner secretary, enfeoffed as duke of Guichang county with a fief of one thousand households, and entrusted with court government.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was swiftly promoted to defender-in-chief and junior inner secretary, enfeoffed as Duke of Guichang with a thousand-household fief, and entrusted with the direction of government.

sentences.zh: 俄遷內史上大夫，進封沛國公，邑五千戶，以其子善願為歸昌公，元琮為永安縣男，又監國史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to senior inner secretary, advanced to duke of Pei state with a fief of five thousand households; his son Shanyuan was made duke of Guichang, Yuancong was made baron of Yong'an county, and he also supervised the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made senior inner secretary and advanced to Duke of Pei with five thousand households; his son Shanyuan became Duke of Guichang and Yuancong Baron of Yong'an, and he was also put in charge of the national history.

sentences.zh: 譯頗專權，時帝幸東京，譯擅取官材，自營私第，坐是複除名為民。

translations.literal: Yi was quite autocratic in power; at the time the emperor was visiting the Eastern Capital; Yi on his own authority took official timber and built a private residence—for this he was again struck from the registers and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Yi grew autocratic; while the emperor was at the Eastern Capital, Yi seized official timber to build a private mansion and was again struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 劉昉數言於帝，帝複召之，顧待如初。

translations.literal: Liu Fang spoke repeatedly to the emperor, and the emperor summoned him again, treating him with regard as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang spoke repeatedly on his behalf, and the emperor recalled him and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 詔領內史事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to head inner secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put him in charge of inner secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖與譯有同學之舊，譯又素知高祖相表有奇，傾心相結。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Jian and Yi had the old tie of schoolmates; Yi had also long known that Yang Jian's physiognomy showed something extraordinary, and gave his heart to bind with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian and Yi had been schoolmates, and Yi had long seen something extraordinary in Yang Jian's bearing; he gave Yang Jian his wholehearted support.

sentences.zh: 至是，高祖為宣帝所忌，情不自安，嘗在永巷私於譯曰：「久願出籓，公所悉也。

translations.literal: At this point Yang Jian was viewed with suspicion by Emperor Xuan and could not feel secure in his feelings; he once in the Eternal Lane spoke privately to Yi, saying, "I have long wished to go out to a frontier post—as you well know.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yang Jian had fallen under Emperor Xuan's suspicion and lived in anxiety; once in the Eternal Lane he confided to Yi, "You know how long I have wished to leave the capital for a post in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 敢布心腹，少留意焉。

translations.literal: I dare lay bare my inmost heart—please give it a little attention."
translations.idiomatic: I lay my heart bare before you—please give me a little help."

sentences.zh: 」譯曰：「以公德望，天下歸心，欲求多福，豈敢忘也。

translations.literal: Yi said, "By your virtue and renown the realm turns its heart to you; if I wish for great blessing, how would I dare forget?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "By your virtue and renown the realm already turns to you; if I seek my own good fortune, how could I forget you?"

sentences.zh: 謹即言之。

translations.literal: I will at once speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: I shall speak of it at once.

sentences.zh: 」時將遣譯南征，譯請元帥。

translations.literal: At that time they were about to send Yi on the southern campaign; Yi requested a commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yi was about to be sent on the southern campaign and asked who should command it.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿意如何？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What is your opinion?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」譯對曰：「若定江東，自非懿戚重臣無以鎮撫。

translations.literal: Yi replied, "If we are to settle the lands east of the Yangzi, none but a close kinsman and weighty minister can pacify and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi answered, "To settle the lands east of the Yangzi will require a kinsman of weight and standing—none other can hold the region.

sentences.zh: 可令隋公行，且為壽陽總管以督軍事。

translations.literal: The Duke of Sui may be sent, and also made governor-general of Shouyang to oversee military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Send the Duke of Sui, and make him governor-general of Shouyang to oversee the campaign."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔以高祖為揚州總管，譯發兵俱會壽陽以伐陳。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued making Yang Jian governor-general of Yangzhou; Yi was to raise troops and together meet at Shouyang to attack Chen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Yang Jian governor-general of Yangzhou; Yi was to raise troops and join him at Shouyang for the campaign against Chen.

sentences.zh: 行有日矣，帝不悆，遂與禦正下大夫劉昉謀，引高祖入受顧托。

translations.literal: The day of departure was near when the emperor fell ill; he then plotted with junior director of the imperial carriage Liu Fang to bring Yang Jian in to receive the dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: The day of departure was near when the emperor fell gravely ill; he and junior director Liu Fang plotted to bring Yang Jian in to receive the regency.

sentences.zh: 既而譯宣詔，文武百官皆受高祖節度。

translations.literal: Soon after Yi proclaimed the edict, and civil and military officials all received Yang Jian's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yi then proclaimed the edict placing all civil and military officials under Yang Jian's command.

sentences.zh: 時禦正中大夫顏之儀與宦者謀，引大將軍宇文仲輔政。

translations.literal: At that time senior director of the imperial carriage Yan Zhiyi plotted with eunuchs to bring in Grand General Yuwen Zhong to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Senior director Yan Zhiyi and certain eunuchs plotted to install Grand General Yuwen Zhong as regent.

sentences.zh: 仲已至禦坐，譯知之，遽率開府楊惠及劉昉、皇甫績、柳裘俱入。

translations.literal: Zhong had already reached the imperial seat when Yi learned of it; he hastily led defender-in-chief Yang Hui together with Liu Fang, Huangfu Ji, and Liu Qiu all in.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong had already reached the throne when Yi learned of it; he rushed in with defender-in-chief Yang Hui, Liu Fang, Huangfu Ji, and Liu Qiu.

sentences.zh: 仲與之儀見譯等，愕然，逡巡欲出，高祖因執之。

translations.literal: Zhong and Zhiyi, seeing Yi and the rest, were startled and hesitated, wishing to withdraw; Yang Jian thereupon seized them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Zhiyi, startled at the sight of Yi and his party, hesitated to flee; Yang Jian seized them.

sentences.zh: 於是矯詔複以譯為內史上大夫。

translations.literal: Thereupon a forged edict again made Yi senior inner secretary.
translations.idiomatic: A forged edict then restored Yi as senior inner secretary.

sentences.zh: 明日，高祖為丞相，拜譯柱國、相府長史、治內史上大夫事。

translations.literal: The next day Yang Jian became chancellor and appointed Yi pillar of state, chief clerk of the chancellor's office, and administrator of senior inner secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when Yang Jian became chancellor, he made Yi pillar of state, chief clerk of the chancellor's office, and head of inner secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為大塚宰，總百揆，以譯兼領天官都府司會，總六府事。

translations.literal: When Yang Jian became Grand Minister of Works overseeing all affairs, he had Yi additionally head the celestial offices directorate and grand coordinator, overseeing the six directorates.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became grand minister of works with oversight of all government, he had Yi also head the celestial offices directorate and coordinate the six ministries.

sentences.zh: 出入臥內，言無不從，賞賜玉帛不可勝計。

translations.literal: Going in and out of the sleeping quarters, none of his words went unheeded; rewards of jade and silk could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: He moved freely in and out of Yang Jian's private quarters; none of his words went unheeded, and rewards of jade and silk poured upon him beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 每出入，以甲士從。

translations.literal: Each time he went out or came in, armored soldiers followed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went abroad, armored guards attended him.

sentences.zh: 拜其子元璹為儀同。

translations.literal: His son Yuansu was appointed attendant of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuansu was made attendant of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 時尉迥、王謙、司馬消難等作亂，高祖逾加親禮。

translations.literal: At that time Yuchi Jiong, Wang Qian, Sima Xiaonan, and others rose in rebellion; Yang Jian added ever more intimate courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong, Wang Qian, Sima Xiaonan, and others rebelled, Yang Jian treated him with still greater favor.

sentences.zh: 俄而進位上柱國，恕以十死。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to senior pillar of state, pardoned up to ten capital offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to senior pillar of state with a pardon extending to ten capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 譯性輕險，不親職務，而髒貨狼籍。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was frivolous and dangerous; he did not attend to his duties, and illicit goods lay scattered in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was frivolous and unreliable, neglected his duties, and his corruption was notorious.

sentences.zh: 高祖陰疏之，然以其有定策功，不忍廢放，陰敕官屬不得白事於譯。

translations.literal: Yang Jian secretly kept him at a distance, yet because he had the merit of settling the policy could not bear to dismiss him; he secretly ordered officials not to report affairs to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian quietly distanced himself, yet because Yi had helped settle the succession he could not bring himself to dismiss him outright; he secretly ordered that no official reports be submitted to Yi.

sentences.zh: 譯猶坐廳事，無所關預。

translations.literal: Yi still sat in the hall of affairs, with nothing to oversee or take part in.
translations.idiomatic: Yi still sat in the council hall, but had nothing to do.

sentences.zh: 譯懼，頓首求解職，高祖寬諭之，接以恩禮。

translations.literal: Yi was afraid, bowed his head and begged to be released from office; Yang Jian comforted him with generous words and received him with favoring courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In fear Yi kowtowed and asked to resign; Yang Jian reassured him kindly and continued to treat him with favor.

sentences.zh: 及上受禪，以上柱國公歸第，賞賜豐厚。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication, he was sent home as senior pillar of state duke, with rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Yi retired to his residence as senior pillar of state with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 進子元璹爵城皋郡公，邑二千戶，元洵永安男。

translations.literal: His son Yuansu was advanced to duke of Chenggao commandery with a fief of two thousand households; Yuanxun was made baron of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuansu was made Duke of Chenggao with two thousand households; Yuanxun was made Baron of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 追贈其父及亡兄二人並為刺史。

translations.literal: His father and two deceased elder brothers were posthumously enfeoffed all as regional governors.
translations.idiomatic: His father and two deceased elder brothers were posthumously made regional governors.

sentences.zh: 譯自以被疏，陰呼道士章醮以祈福助，其婢奏譯厭蠱左道。

translations.literal: Yi, considering himself kept at a distance, secretly summoned Daoist priests for liturgies and offerings to seek blessing and aid; his maid reported that Yi practiced curse-magic and heterodox ways.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking himself cast aside, Yi secretly had Daoist priests perform rites for his benefit; a maid reported that he practiced sorcery and heterodox arts.

sentences.zh: 上謂譯曰：「我不負公，此何意也？

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yi, "I have not failed you—what is the meaning of this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to him, "I have not wronged you—what is the meaning of this?"

sentences.zh: 」譯無以對。

translations.literal: Yi had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had no answer.

sentences.zh: 譯又與母別居，為憲司所劾，由是除名。

translations.literal: Yi also lived apart from his mother and was impeached by the censorate; for this his name was struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: He was also living apart from his mother; the censorate impeached him, and he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「譯嘉謀良策，寂爾無聞，鬻獄賣官，沸騰盈耳。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Yi's fine counsel and good stratagems are heard no more in silence; selling judgments and vending offices—the noise boils over and fills the ears."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "Fine counsel from Yi is nowhere to be heard, while the sale of offices and judgments fills every ear."

sentences.zh: 若留之於世，在人為不道之臣，戮之於朝，入地為不孝之鬼。

translations.literal: If he is kept in the world, among the living he is an unprincipled minister; if executed at court, in the earth he is an unfilial ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Kept among the living he is an unprincipled minister; executed at court he becomes an unfilial ghost in the underworld.

sentences.zh: 有累幽顯，無以置之，宜賜以《孝經》，令其熟讀。

translations.literal: He burdens both the hidden and the manifest; there is no way to place him—he should be given the Classic of Filial Piety and made to read it thoroughly."
translations.idiomatic: He shames both the living and the dead; there is no fitting punishment—let him be given the Classic of Filial Piety and made to study it well."

sentences.zh: 」仍遣與母共居。

translations.literal: He was still sent to dwell with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was nevertheless ordered to live with his mother again.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔譯參撰律令，複授開府、隆州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered Yi to take part in compiling statutes and ordinances, and he was again appointed defender-in-chief and governor of Long prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was ordered to help compile the law code and was again made defender-in-chief and governor of Long prefecture.

sentences.zh: 請還治疾，有詔征之，見於醴泉宮。

translations.literal: He requested leave to return and treat illness; an edict summoned him, and he was received at Liquan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to return home to treat an illness; the emperor summoned him and received him at Liquan Palace.

sentences.zh: 上賜宴甚歡，因謂譯曰：「貶退已久，情相矜湣。

translations.literal: The emperor gave a feast with great pleasure and therefore said to Yi, "Your demotion and withdrawal have been long; in feeling I sympathize and pity you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave a joyful feast and told him, "You have been in disgrace a long time, and I have felt pity for you."

sentences.zh: 」於是複爵沛國公，位上柱國。

translations.literal: Thereupon his title of Duke of Pei was restored and he held the rank of senior pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: His title of Duke of Pei and rank of senior pillar of state were restored.

sentences.zh: 上顧謂侍臣曰：「鄭譯與朕同生共死，間關危難，興言念此，何日忘之！

translations.literal: The emperor turned and said to attending ministers, "Zheng Yi and I shared life and death through perilous straits; raising the subject and thinking on this—what day could I forget it!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his attendants and said, "Zheng Yi shared life and death with me through every danger; whenever I think of it, how could I ever forget!"

sentences.zh: 」譯因奉觴上壽。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon offered the cup and wished long life.
translations.idiomatic: Yi raised his cup and offered a toast for the emperor's long life.

sentences.zh: 上令內史令李德林立作詔書，高熲戲謂譯曰：「筆幹。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered inner secretariat director Li Delin to draft an edict on the spot; Gao Jiong jested to Yi, saying, "Pen and ink."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had inner secretariat director Li Delin draft an edict on the spot; Gao Jiong teased Yi, saying, "Here's your brush fee."

sentences.zh: 」譯答曰：「出為方嶽，杖策言歸，不得一錢，何以潤筆。

translations.literal: Yi replied, "Going out as a regional lord, staff in hand speaking of return—I did not get a single cash; with what shall I moisten the brush?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi answered, "Sent out as a provincial governor, I returned without a single cash to my name—what fee is there to moisten the brush?"

sentences.zh: 」上大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔譯參議樂事。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered Yi to take part in deliberating music affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was ordered to take part in deliberations on court music.

sentences.zh: 譯以周代七聲廢缺，自大隋受命，禮樂宜新，更修七始之義，名曰《樂府聲調》，凡八篇。

translations.literal: Yi held that under Zhou the seven tones were abandoned and deficient; since Great Sui received the mandate, rites and music should be made new; he again revised the meaning of the seven beginnings, titled Music Bureau Tonal Patterns, eight sections in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yi held that the seven tones of Zhou music had fallen into disuse; with the founding of Sui, rites and music should be renewed. He revised the theory of the seven tonal origins in a work entitled Music Bureau Tonal Patterns in eight sections.

sentences.zh: 奏之，上嘉美焉。

translations.literal: He presented it; the emperor praised and admired it.
translations.idiomatic: He presented it to the throne, and the emperor praised it highly.

sentences.zh: 俄遷岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor of Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made governor of Qi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在職歲餘，複奉詔定樂於太常，前後所論樂事，語在《音律志》。

translations.literal: In office more than a year, he again received an edict to fix music at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; music matters discussed before and after are recorded in the Treatise on Pitch and Regulation.
translations.idiomatic: After a year in office he was again ordered to fix the court music at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his discussions on music are recorded in the Treatise on Pitch and Regulation.

sentences.zh: 上勞譯曰：「律令則公定之，音樂則公正之。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted Yi, saying, "Statutes and ordinances you have fixed; music you have rectified.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, saying, "You fixed the law code, and you have set the music right.

sentences.zh: 禮樂律令，公居其三，良足美也。

translations.literal: Of rites, music, statutes, and ordinances, you hold three of them—truly enough to admire."
translations.idiomatic: Of ritual, music, and law you hold three parts—a fine achievement indeed."

sentences.zh: 」於是還岐州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to Qi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開皇十一年，以疾卒官，時年五十二，上遣使弔祭焉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang he died in office of illness, aged fifty-two; the emperor sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang he died in office of illness at fifty-two; the emperor sent envoys to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 諡曰達。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Da.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Da.

sentences.zh: 子元璹嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yuansu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuansu succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 煬帝初立，五等悉除，以譯佐命元功，詔追改封譯莘公，以元璹襲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang first took the throne, the five ranks were all abolished; because Yi had the founding merit of assisting the mandate, an edict posthumously changed his enfeoffment to duke of Shen, and Yuansu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang first took the throne the five noble ranks were abolished; because Yi had been a founding supporter, an edict posthumously changed his title to Duke of Shen, which Yuansu inherited.

sentences.zh: 元璹初為驃騎將軍，後轉武賁郎將，數以軍功進位右光祿大夫，遷右候衛將軍。

translations.literal: Yuansu at first was general of the swift cavalry, later transferred to captain of the martial guard, and repeatedly for military merit was advanced to right grand master for splendid happiness, then transferred to right guard of the palace gate general.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu first served as general of swift cavalry, then as captain of the martial guard; for repeated military merit he rose to right grand master for splendid happiness and then to right guard of the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 大業末，出為文城太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he went out as governor of Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daye era he was sent out as governor of Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 及義兵起，義將張倫略地至文城，元璹以城歸之。

translations.literal: When the righteous armies rose, righteous general Zhang Lun overran the territory as far as Wencheng; Yuansu surrendered the city to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the loyalist armies rose, Zhang Lun advanced as far as Wencheng, and Yuansu surrendered the city to him.

sentences.zh: 柳裘柳裘，字茂和，河東解人，齊司空世隆之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Qiu, Liu Qiu, styled Maohe, was a native of Jie in Hedong, a great-grandson of Qi Minister of Works Shi Long.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu, whose style name was Maohe, was a native of Jie in Hedong commandery and a great-grandson of Qi Minister of Works Liu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 祖惔，梁尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan was Liang Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tan had served as Liang Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父明，太子舍人、義興太守。

translations.literal: His father Ming was crown prince attendant and governor of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ming had served as crown prince attendant and governor of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 裘少聰慧，弱冠有令名，在梁仕曆尚書郎、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Qiu in youth was clever and intelligent; at twenty he had a fine reputation; in Liang he served through several posts as secretariat gentleman and commandant of the horse escort for the imperial son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was clever as a boy and by twenty enjoyed a fine reputation; under Liang he served as a secretariat gentleman and imperial son-in-law commandant.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝為魏軍所逼，遣裘請和于魏。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang, pressed by Wei armies, sent Qiu to seek peace with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was hard pressed by Wei forces, he sent Qiu to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 俄而江陵陷，遂入關中。

translations.literal: Soon Jiangling fell, and he thereupon entered the Pass region.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiangling fell, and he entered the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 周明、武間，自麟趾學士累遷太子侍讀，封昌樂縣侯。

translations.literal: Between the Ming and Wu reigns of Zhou, from Linzhi academician he was repeatedly promoted to crown prince reader-in-waiting and enfeoffed as marquis of Changle county.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ming and Wu of Zhou he rose from Linzhi academician to crown prince reader-in-waiting and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changle.

sentences.zh: 後除天官府都上士。

translations.literal: Later he was made senior gentleman of the celestial offices directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made senior gentleman of the celestial offices directorate.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，拜儀同三司，進爵為公，轉禦飾大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he was appointed attendant of the third rank, advanced in title to duke, and transferred to director of imperial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was made attendant of the third rank, advanced to duke, and made director of imperial regalia.

sentences.zh: 及帝不悆，留侍禁中，與劉昉、韋䴙、皇甫績同謀，引高祖入總萬機。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, he remained to attend in the inner palace, plotted together with Liu Fang, Wei Mu, and Huangfu Ji, and brought Yang Jian in to oversee all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor grew gravely ill, he stayed in the inner palace and, with Liu Fang, Wei Mu, and Huangfu Ji, plotted to bring Yang Jian in to take charge of government.

sentences.zh: 高祖固讓不許。

translations.literal: Yang Jian firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian repeatedly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 裘進曰：「時不可再，機不可失，今事已然，宜早定大計。

translations.literal: Qiu advanced and said, "The time cannot come twice, the opportunity cannot be lost; now the affair is already settled—you should early fix the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu urged him, saying, "Time does not come twice, opportunity does not wait; the matter is already decided—you must settle the great plan at once.

sentences.zh: 天與不取，反受其咎，如更遷延，恐貽後悔。

translations.literal: What Heaven gives and you do not take, you will instead receive its blame; if you further delay, I fear you will leave regret."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's gift refused brings Heaven's blame; further delay will bring regret."

sentences.zh: 」高祖從之。

translations.literal: Yang Jian followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian yielded and accepted.

sentences.zh: 進位上開府，拜內史大夫，委以機密。

translations.literal: He was advanced to senior defender-in-chief, appointed senior inner secretary, and entrusted with secrets.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to senior defender-in-chief and senior inner secretary and entrusted with confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 及尉迥作亂，天下騷動，并州總管李穆頗懷猶豫，高祖令裘往喻之。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled and the realm was in turmoil, Bingzhou governor-general Li Mu harbored considerable hesitation; Yang Jian ordered Qiu to go and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled and the realm was unsettled, Bingzhou governor-general Li Mu wavered; Yang Jian sent Qiu to win him over.

sentences.zh: 裘見穆，盛陳利害，穆甚悅，遂歸心于高祖。

translations.literal: Qiu saw Mu and set forth benefit and harm at length; Mu was greatly pleased and thereupon gave his heart to Yang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu laid out the stakes before Li Mu, who was persuaded and gave Yang Jian his wholehearted support.

sentences.zh: 後以奉使功，賜彩三百匹，金九環帶一腰。

translations.literal: Later, for merit on a mission, he was given three hundred bolts of colored silk and one belt of gold with nine rings.
translations.idiomatic: For his service as envoy he was rewarded with three hundred bolts of silk and a gold belt with nine rings.

sentences.zh: 時司馬消難阻兵安陸，又令喻之，未到而消難奔陳。

translations.literal: At that time Sima Xiaonan held troops at Anlu in obstruction; he was again ordered to instruct him, but before arriving Xiaonan fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiaonan was then holding Anlu with armed force; Qiu was sent to reason with him, but before he arrived Xiaonan had fled to Chen.

sentences.zh: 高祖即令裘隨便安集淮南，賜馬及雜物。

translations.literal: Yang Jian at once ordered Qiu to settle Huainan as opportunity allowed and gave him horses and various goods.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian then had him pacify Huainan as circumstances allowed and gave him horses and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，進位大將軍，拜許州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was advanced to grand general and appointed governor of Xu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he was made grand general and governor of Xu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在官清簡，吏民懷之。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and simple; officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was pure and simple, and officials and commoners alike cherished him.

sentences.zh: 複轉曹州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to governor of Cao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to governor of Cao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其後上思裘定策功，欲加榮秩，將征之，顧問朝臣曰：「曹州刺史何當入朝？

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor recalled Qiu's merit in settling the policy, wished to add honor and rank, and was about to summon him; he turned to court ministers and asked, "When will the governor of Cao prefecture come to court?"
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor, mindful of Qiu's role in settling the succession, meant to honor him further and summon him to court; he asked his ministers, "When will the governor of Cao come to court?"

sentences.zh: 」或對曰：「即今冬也。

translations.literal: Someone replied, "This very winter."
translations.idiomatic: One replied, "This winter."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 裘尋卒，高祖傷惜者久之，諡曰安。

translations.literal: Qiu soon died; Yang Jian mourned and cherished his memory for a long time; his posthumous title was An.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu soon died; the emperor mourned him long; his posthumous name was An.

sentences.zh: 子惠童嗣。

translations.literal: His son Huitong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huitong succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 皇甫績皇甫績，字功明，安定朝那人也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Ji, Huangfu Ji, styled Gongming, was a native of Chaona in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Ji, whose style name was Gongming, was a native of Chaona in Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖穆，魏隴東太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mu was Wei governor of Longdong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mu had served as Wei governor of Longdong.

sentences.zh: 父道，周湖州刺史、雍州都督。

translations.literal: His father Dao was Zhou governor of Hu prefecture and area commander of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dao had served as Zhou governor of Hu prefecture and area commander of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 績三歲而孤，為外祖韋孝寬所鞠養。

translations.literal: Ji was orphaned at three and was reared by his maternal grandfather Wei Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at three, he was raised by his maternal grandfather Wei Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 嘗與諸外兄博奕，孝寬以其惰業，督以嚴訓，湣績孤幼，特舍之。

translations.literal: He once gambled with his various cousins by the maternal line; Xiaokuan, because of his lazy studies, urged him with stern instruction, yet pitied Ji as orphaned and young and specially spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, gambling with his cousins, he was sternly rebuked by Xiaokuan for neglecting his studies; pitying the orphan boy, Xiaokuan let the matter pass.

sentences.zh: 績歎曰：「我無庭訓，養於外氏，不能克躬勵己，何以成立？

translations.literal: Ji sighed and said, "I have no instruction in the family hall, am reared in the outer clan—if I cannot restrain myself and urge myself on, how can I be established?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji sighed, "I lost my father early and was raised in my grandfather's house; if I cannot discipline myself, how can I amount to anything?"

sentences.zh: 」深自感激，命左右自杖三十。

translations.literal: Deeply moved in himself, he ordered his attendants to beat him thirty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply shamed, he ordered his attendants to flog him thirty strokes.

sentences.zh: 孝寬聞而對之流涕。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan heard and faced him with streaming tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaokuan heard of it, he wept before him.

sentences.zh: 於是精心好學，略涉經史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he applied his mind to loving learning and dipped slightly into the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he devoted himself to study and gained some acquaintance with the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 周武帝為魯公時，引為侍讀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was Duke of Lu, he was brought in as reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu was still Duke of Lu, Ji was made his reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 建德初，轉宮尹中士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande he was transferred to palace steward gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiande era he became palace steward gentleman.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗避暑雲陽宮，時宣帝為太子監國。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once took summer ease at Yunyang Palace; at that time Emperor Xuan as crown prince oversaw the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu was summering at Yunyang Palace, the crown prince—later Emperor Xuan—was regent in the capital.

sentences.zh: 衛剌王作亂，城門已閉，百僚多有遁者。

translations.literal: Prince Wei of Wei rebelled; the city gates were already shut, and many among the hundred officials had fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei rebelled, the city gates were shut and many officials had fled.

sentences.zh: 績聞難赴之，於玄武門遇皇太子，太子下樓執績手，悲喜交集。

translations.literal: Ji heard of the crisis and hurried to it; at the Xuanwu Gate he met the crown prince; the crown prince came down the stairs and grasped Ji's hand, grief and joy intermingled.
translations.idiomatic: Ji heard of the crisis and rushed to the palace; at the Xuanwu Gate he met the crown prince, who came down to take his hand, joy and grief mingled in his face.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉之，遷小宮尹。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and commended this, promoting him to junior palace steward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyalty and made him junior palace steward.

sentences.zh: 宣政初，錄前後功，封義陽縣男，拜畿伯下大夫，累轉禦正下大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanzheng, recording merit before and after, he was enfeoffed as baron of Yiyang county, appointed capital district junior grand master, and repeatedly transferred to junior director of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xuanzheng his past services were recognized; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yiyang, made capital district junior grand master, and later junior director of the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 宣帝崩，高祖總己，績有力焉，語在《鄭譯傳》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Yang Jian took personal charge of affairs; Ji had strength in this—the account is in the Biography of Zheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan died and Yang Jian took charge, Ji played an important part, as told in the biography of Zheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 加位上開府，轉內史中大夫，進封郡公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to senior defender-in-chief, transferred to inner secretary grand master, promoted to commandery duke with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made senior defender-in-chief and inner secretary grand master, then advanced to commandery duke with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 尋拜大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，出為豫州刺史，增邑通前二千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he went out as governor of Yu prefecture, his fief increased to two thousand five hundred households including previous holdings.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he was sent out as governor of Yu prefecture, his fief rising to twenty-five hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 尋拜都官尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 後數載，轉晉州刺史，將之官，稽首而言曰：「臣實庸鄙，無益于國，每思犯難以報國恩。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to governor of Jin prefecture; about to take office, he bowed his head and said, "Your servant is truly mediocre and base, of no benefit to the state; I ever think to brave hardship to repay the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later, as he was leaving to take up the governorship of Jin prefecture, he kowtowed and said, "I am a mediocre man who has done little for the state; I have long wished to risk myself in its service.

sentences.zh: 今偽陳尚存，以臣度之，有三可滅。

translations.literal: Now false Chen still exists; by your servant's estimate, there are three reasons it can be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: False Chen still stands; in my judgment there are three reasons it can be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 」上問其故，'績答曰：「大吞小，一也；

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; Ji replied, "The great swallows the small—one;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; Ji answered, "First, the great swallows the small;

sentences.zh: 以有道伐無道，二也；

translations.literal: with the Way one attacks the wayless—two;
translations.idiomatic: second, the righteous attacks the unrighteous;

sentences.zh: 納叛臣蕭岩，於我有詞，三也。

translations.literal: harboring the rebel minister Xiao Yan, we have cause against them—three."
translations.idiomatic: third, they harbor the rebel Xiao Yan, which gives us just cause."

sentences.zh: 陛下若命鷹揚之將，臣請預戎行，展絲發之效。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty orders soaring-hawk generals, your servant asks to join the campaign and display an effort no greater than a hair's breadth."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sends forth his boldest generals, I beg to join the campaign, however small my contribution may be."

sentences.zh: 」上嘉其壯志，勞而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his bold will, comforted him, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his spirit, comforted him, and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，拜蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was appointed governor of Su prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was conquered, he was made governor of Su prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高智慧等作亂江南，州民顧子元發兵應之，因以攻績，相持八旬。

translations.literal: Gao Zhihui and others rebelled in Jiangnan; the prefecture's people Gu Ziyuan raised troops in response and thereby attacked Ji; they faced each other for eighty days.
