translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled in the south, Gu Ziyuan of the prefecture rallied troops to join them and besieged Ji for eighty days.

sentences.zh: 子元素感績恩，於冬至日遣使奉牛酒。

translations.literal: Ziyuan was moved by Ji's kindness and on the winter solstice sent envoys presenting oxen and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Touched by Ji's past kindness, Ziyuan sent envoys on the winter solstice with oxen and wine.

sentences.zh: 績遺子元書曰：「皇帝握符受籙，合極通靈，受揖讓于唐、虞，棄干戈于湯、武。

translations.literal: Ji sent Ziyuan a letter, saying, "The emperor holds the tally and receives the register, unites the pole and communes with spirits, received abdication from Tang and Yu, and cast aside weapons like Tang and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji wrote to Ziyuan: "The emperor holds Heaven's mandate, communes with the spirits, received the abdication as Tang and Yu did, and laid down arms as Tang of Shang and King Wu did.

sentences.zh: 東逾蟠木，方朔所未窮西盡流沙，張騫所不至。

translations.literal: East he passes Panmu, which Dongfang Shuo did not exhaust; west he reaches the drifting sands, where Zhang Qian did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: His realm stretches east beyond Panmu, farther than Dongfang Shuo ever roamed, and west to the drifting sands, where Zhang Qian never ventured.

sentences.zh: 玄漠黃龍之外，交臂來王；

translations.literal: Beyond the dark desert and Yellow Dragon, they fold arms and come as kings;
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the northern deserts, peoples fold their arms in submission;

sentences.zh: 蔥嶺、榆關之表，屈膝請吏。

translations.literal: outside Congling and Yuguan Pass, they bend the knee and request officials.
translations.idiomatic: west of Congling and Yuguan, they kneel and beg for imperial officials.

sentences.zh: 曩者偽陳獨阻聲教，江東士民困於荼毒。

translations.literal: Formerly false Chen alone blocked the transforming voice; the gentry and people east of the Yangzi suffered under bitter poison.
translations.idiomatic: Only false Chen once blocked the imperial transforming influence, and the people of the lower Yangzi suffered under its cruelty.

sentences.zh: 皇天輔仁，假手朝廷，聊申薄伐，應時瓦解。

translations.literal: August Heaven assists the humane; lending its hand through the court, we briefly launched a modest punitive campaign, and it collapsed at the season.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven aided the humane cause; the court sent a brief punitive expedition, and Chen collapsed at once.

sentences.zh: 金陵百姓，死而復生，吳、會臣民，白骨還肉。

translations.literal: The common people of Jinling were dead and lived again; the subjects of Wu and Kuai, white bones regained flesh.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jinling were raised from the dead; in Wu and Kuai, bleached bones lived again.

sentences.zh: 唯當懷音感德，行歌擊壤，豈宜自同吠主，翻成反噬。

translations.literal: They should only cherish kindness and feel virtue, walk singing and strike the earth in joy—how should they make themselves like dogs that bark at their master and turn to bite back?
translations.idiomatic: They ought to cherish the emperor's grace and sing his praise—how can they bark at their master like curs and turn to bite the hand that fed them?

sentences.zh: 卿非吾民，何須酒禮？

translations.literal: You, sir, are not our people—why need wine and ritual gifts?
translations.idiomatic: You are no subject of mine—why send wine and gifts?

sentences.zh: 吾是隋將，何容外交？

translations.literal: I am a Sui general—how can foreign dealings be allowed?
translations.idiomatic: I am a general of Sui—how can I accept overtures from the enemy?

sentences.zh: 易子析骸，未能相告，況是足食足兵，高城深塹，坐待強援，綽有餘力。

translations.literal: Exchanging children and splitting bones to eat—they could not tell each other; how much more when there is full food and full troops, high walls and deep moats, sitting to await strong reinforcements, with strength to spare.
translations.idiomatic: When men exchange children and eat each other's flesh, they cannot help one another—yet you have ample food and troops, high walls and deep moats, and sit waiting for reinforcements with strength to spare.

sentences.zh: 何勞踵輕敝之俗，作虛偽之辭，欲阻誠臣之心，徒惑驍雄之志。

translations.literal: Why trouble to follow light and base custom, make false and empty words, wish to block a loyal minister's heart, and vainly confuse bold heroes' resolve?
translations.idiomatic: Why follow base custom with false words, hoping to shake a loyal minister's heart and confuse brave men's resolve?

sentences.zh: 以此見期，必不可得。

translations.literal: To expect this of me is surely impossible to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Such expectations of me are vain.

sentences.zh: 卿宜善思活路，曉諭黎元，能早改迷，失道非遠。

translations.literal: You, sir, should well consider a path to life, enlighten the black-haired people; if you can early turn from error, straying from the Way is not far to return.
translations.idiomatic: Consider your path to survival, enlighten your people—if you turn back soon, you are not far from the right road."

sentences.zh: 」子元得書，於城下頓首陳謝。

translations.literal: Ziyuan received the letter and below the wall bowed his head and declared his apology.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyuan received the letter and kowtowed in submission below the wall.

sentences.zh: 楊素援兵至，合擊破之。

translations.literal: Yang Su's relief troops arrived; joining forces they broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Su's relief force arrived, they joined in and defeated the rebels.

sentences.zh: 拜信州總管、十二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor-general of Xin prefecture and military affairs over twelve prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor-general of Xin and commander of military affairs for twelve prefectures.

sentences.zh: 俄以病乞骸骨，詔征還京，賜以禦藥，中使相望，顧問不絕。

translations.literal: Soon, on grounds of illness, he begged to yield his bones; an edict summoned him back to the capital, gave him imperial medicines, palace envoys followed one another in sight, and inquiries were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to retire on grounds of illness; the emperor summoned him to the capital, sent imperial physicians, and palace envoys followed one another with inquiries.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，時年五十二。

translations.literal: He died at home, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 諡曰安。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was An.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was An.

sentences.zh: 子偲嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cai succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 大業之世，官至尚書主爵郎。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he reached the post of secretariat director of enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he rose to director of enfeoffments in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 韋䴙者，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Wei Mu was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mu was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 仕周內史大夫。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as inner secretary grand master.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Zhou inner secretary grand master.

sentences.zh: 高祖以䴙有定策之功，累遷上柱國，封普安郡公。

translations.literal: Yang Jian, because Mu had the merit of settling the policy, repeatedly promoted him to senior pillar of state and enfeoffed him as duke of Pu'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Mu had helped settle the succession, Yang Jian repeatedly promoted him to senior pillar of state and enfeoffed him as Duke of Pu'an.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，卒于蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he died in office as governor of Pu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang he died in office as governor of Pu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 盧賁盧賁，字子徵，涿郡范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Ben, Lu Ben, styled Zizheng, was a native of Fanyang in Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ben, whose style name was Zizheng, was a native of Fanyang in Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 父光，周開府、燕郡公。

translations.literal: His father Guang was Zhou defender-in-chief and Duke of Yan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang had been Zhou defender-in-chief and Duke of Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 賁略涉書記，頗解鐘律。

translations.literal: Ben dipped slightly into writing and records and understood bells and pitch pipes rather well.
translations.idiomatic: Ben had some education in letters and was well versed in music theory.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，襲爵燕郡公，邑一千九百戶。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou he inherited the title Duke of Yan commandery with a fief of one thousand nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he inherited the title Duke of Yan with a fief of nineteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後曆魯陽太守、太子小宮尹、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later he passed through governor of Luyang, junior palace steward of the crown prince, and attendant of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Luyang, junior palace steward to the crown prince, and attendant of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 平齊有功，增邑四百戶，轉司武上士。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Qi his fief was increased by four hundred households; he was transferred to senior martial affairs gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in the conquest of Qi his fief was increased by four hundred households and he was made senior martial affairs gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時高祖為大司武，賁知高祖為非常人，深自推結。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Jian was Grand Minister of Martial Affairs; Ben knew Yang Jian was no ordinary man and deeply gave himself to bind with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was Grand Minister of Martial Affairs, Ben recognized him as no ordinary man and gave him his wholehearted allegiance.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，加開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was added as defender-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was made defender-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 及高祖初被顧托，群情未一，乃引賁置於左右。

translations.literal: When Yang Jian was first entrusted with the dying charge, popular feeling was not united; he therefore drew Ben and placed him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian first received the regency and opinion was still divided, he kept Ben close at his side.

sentences.zh: 高祖將之東第，百官皆不知所去。

translations.literal: Yang Jian was about to go to the Eastern Residence; the hundred officials all did not know where they were going.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was about to go to the Eastern Residence, the officials did not know what course to take.

sentences.zh: 高祖潛令賁部伍仗衛，因召公卿而謂曰：「欲求富貴者，當相隨來。

translations.literal: Yang Jian secretly ordered Ben to array troops and armed guards; he then summoned the nobles and said, "Those who wish to seek wealth and honor should follow and come."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian secretly ordered Ben to muster armed guards, then summoned the nobles and said, "Whoever seeks wealth and honor should follow me."

sentences.zh: 」往往偶語，欲有去就。

translations.literal: Here and there they spoke in pairs, wishing to decide whether to go or stay.
translations.idiomatic: Many murmured among themselves, uncertain whether to go or stay.

sentences.zh: 賁嚴兵而至，眾莫敢動。

translations.literal: Ben came with stern troops; the crowd dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: Ben arrived with stern-faced troops, and none dared stir.

sentences.zh: 出崇陽門，至東宮，門者拒不內。

translations.literal: They went out the Chongyang Gate and reached the Eastern Palace; the gatekeepers refused to admit them.
translations.idiomatic: They went out through the Chongyang Gate to the Eastern Palace, but the gatekeepers refused them entry.

sentences.zh: 賁諭之，不去，瞋目叱之，門者遂卻。

translations.literal: Ben instructed them, but they did not leave; he glared and shouted at them, and the gatekeepers then drew back.
translations.idiomatic: Ben reasoned with them in vain, then glared and shouted; the gatekeepers fell back.

sentences.zh: 既而高祖得入。

translations.literal: Soon after Yang Jian was able to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was then able to enter.

sentences.zh: 賁恆典宿衛，後承問，進說曰：「周曆已盡，天人之望，實歸明公，願早應天順民也。

translations.literal: Ben constantly presided over night guard; later, when addressed, he advanced and said, "The Zhou mandate is exhausted; the hope of Heaven and man truly returns to Your Excellency—I wish you would early respond to Heaven and accord with the people."
translations.idiomatic: Ben regularly commanded the night guard; later, when Yang Jian spoke with him, he urged, "The Zhou mandate is spent; Heaven and the people look to you—take the throne and respond to their will."

sentences.zh: 天與不取，反受其咎。

translations.literal: What Heaven gives and you do not take, you will instead receive its blame.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's gift refused brings Heaven's blame.

sentences.zh: 」高祖甚然之。

translations.literal: Yang Jian greatly approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，命賁清宮，因典宿衛。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he ordered Ben to clear the palace and thereby put him in charge of night guard.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, he had Ben secure the palace and placed him in command of the night guard.

sentences.zh: 賁於是奏改周代旗幟，更為嘉名。

translations.literal: Ben thereupon memorialized to change the banners of Zhou and give them finer names.
translations.idiomatic: Ben then memorialized to replace the Zhou banners with new ones bearing auspicious names.

sentences.zh: 其青龍、騶虞、硃雀、玄武、千秋、萬歲之旗，皆賁所創也。

translations.literal: The banners Azure Dragon, Zouyu, Vermilion Bird, Dark Warrior, Thousand Autumns, and Ten Thousand Years were all created by Ben.
translations.idiomatic: The banners of the Azure Dragon, Zouyu, Vermilion Bird, Dark Warrior, Thousand Autumns, and Ten Thousand Years were all his creation.

sentences.zh: 尋拜散騎常侍，兼太子左庶子、左領軍、右將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed attendant cavalier at court, and concurrently left heir apparent of the crown prince, left commander of the palace gate guard, and right general.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made attendant cavalier at court, and concurrently left heir apparent to the crown prince, left commander of the palace gate guard, and right general.

sentences.zh: 時高熲、蘇威共掌朝政，賁甚不平之。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Jiong and Su Wei jointly held court government; Ben was very resentful of this.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong and Su Wei then shared control of government, to Ben's great resentment.

sentences.zh: 柱國劉昉時被疏忌，賁因諷昉及上柱國元諧、李詢、華州刺史張賓等，謀黜熲、威，五人相與輔政。

translations.literal: Pillar of state Liu Fang was then kept at a distance and viewed with suspicion; Ben therefore exhorted Fang and senior pillar of state Yuan Xie, Li Xun, governor of Hua prefecture Zhang Bin, and others to plot removing Jiong and Wei—the five men together would assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, then under suspicion, was enlisted by Ben, who also won over Yuan Xie, Li Xun, and Zhang Bin, governor of Hua, to a plot to oust Gao Jiong and Su Wei and govern through a five-man junta.

sentences.zh: 又以晉王上之愛子，謀行廢立。

translations.literal: They also, because the Prince of Jin was the emperor's beloved son, plotted to carry out deposition and establishment.
translations.idiomatic: They also plotted to displace the heir in favor of the Prince of Jin, the emperor's favorite son.

sentences.zh: 複私謂皇太子曰：「賁將數謁殿下，恐為上所譴，願察區區之心。

translations.literal: He again privately said to the crown prince, "Ben will several times call on Your Highness; I fear the emperor will reproach this—I wish you would perceive my humble heart."
translations.idiomatic: He also told the crown prince privately, "Ben will visit you often; the emperor may take offense—please understand my sincere intent."

sentences.zh: 」謀泄，上窮治其事。

translations.literal: The plot leaked; the emperor prosecuted it to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot leaked, the emperor investigated it thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 昉等委罪於賓、賁，公卿奏二人坐當死。

translations.literal: Fang and the rest shifted blame onto Bin and Ben; the nobles memorialized that the two men's offense warranted death.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and the others shifted blame to Bin and Ben; the nobles memorialized that both deserved death.

sentences.zh: 上以龍潛之舊，不忍加誅，並除名為民。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of old ties from before he rose, could not bear to execute them and struck both from the registers, making them commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering their old ties from before he took power, the emperor spared their lives and struck them from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 賓未幾卒。

translations.literal: Bin soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Bin died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，賁複爵位，檢校太常卿。

translations.literal: After more than a year Ben's noble rank was restored and he was made acting Court of Imperial Sacrifices director.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Ben's rank was restored and he was made acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 賁以古樂宮懸七八，損益不同，歷代通儒，議無定準，於是上表曰：「殷人以上，通用五音，周武克殷，得鶉火、天駟之應，其音用七。

translations.literal: Ben, because in ancient music the palace suspended bells were seven or eight with differing additions and subtractions, and successive generations of accomplished scholars had debated without fixed standard, thereupon submitted a memorial, saying, "From the Yin and above, five tones were generally used; King Wu of Zhou conquered Yin and obtained the responses of Quail Fire and Heavenly Team—their tones used seven.
translations.idiomatic: Ben noted that ancient court music used seven or eight suspended chime-bells, with differing arrangements, and that scholars through the ages had never agreed; he memorialized, saying, "From the Yin dynasty onward five tones were standard; when King Wu of Zhou conquered Yin he took seven tones, matching the omens of Quail Fire and the Heavenly Team.

sentences.zh: 漢興，加應鐘，故十六枚而在一虡。

translations.literal: When Han rose, Yingzhong was added, so sixteen pieces hung on one frame.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han, Yingzhong was added, making sixteen bells on one frame.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注《周禮》，二八十六為虡。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan annotated the Rites of Zhou: two times eight sixteen make a frame.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Rites of Zhou reads two eights—sixteen bells on one frame.

sentences.zh: 此則七八之義，其來遠矣。

translations.literal: This then is the meaning of seven and eight—its origin is far off.
translations.idiomatic: The tradition of seven and eight tones thus reaches far back.

sentences.zh: 然世有沿革，用舍不同，至周武帝，複改懸七，以林鐘為宮。

translations.literal: Yet ages have continuity and change, use and discard differ; down to Emperor Wu of Zhou, he again changed the suspension to seven, taking Forest Bell as the keynote.
translations.idiomatic: Yet usage changed with each age; under Emperor Wu of Zhou the suspension was again set at seven, with Forest Bell as the keynote.

sentences.zh: 夫樂者，治之本也，故移風易俗，莫善於樂，是以吳劄觀而辯興亡。

translations.literal: Now music is the root of governance; therefore in transforming customs and changing habits nothing is better than music—thus Wu Zha observed it and distinguished rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Music is the foundation of governance; nothing transforms custom like music—hence Wu Zha judged a state's rise or fall by its music.

sentences.zh: 然則樂也者，所以動天地，感鬼神，情發於聲，治亂斯應。

translations.literal: Thus music is what moves Heaven and earth and stirs ghosts and spirits; feeling issues in sound, and order and disorder thereupon respond.
translations.idiomatic: Music moves Heaven and earth and touches spirits; emotion sounds forth in it, and order or chaos answers in turn.

sentences.zh: 周武以林鐘為宮，蓋將亡之徵也。

translations.literal: Zhou Wu taking Forest Bell as keynote was roughly a sign of impending ruin.
translations.idiomatic: That Zhou took Forest Bell as keynote was itself a sign of a dynasty about to perish.

sentences.zh: 且林鐘之管，即黃鐘下生之義。

translations.literal: Moreover the pipe of Forest Bell is precisely the principle of Yellow Bell generating below.
translations.idiomatic: Forest Bell is generated below from Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘，君也，而生於臣，明為皇家九五之應。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell is the ruler, yet is generated in the minister—clearly the response of the imperial house to the Nine-Five.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell is the ruler's tone, yet arises from the minister's—plainly an omen that the imperial house would attain the throne.

sentences.zh: 又陰者臣也，而居君位，更顯國家登極之祥。

translations.literal: Again, yin is the minister yet occupies the ruler's position—still more displaying the auspice of the state's ascending the pinnacle.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, the minister's element, held the ruler's place—a further sign that the dynasty would take the throne.

sentences.zh: 斯實冥數相符，非關人事。

translations.literal: This truly matched the dark tally and was not connected to human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: This was destiny's working, not mere human contrivance.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下握圖禦宇，道邁前王，功成作樂，煥乎曩策。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty holds the chart and governs the realm, your Way surpassing former kings; merit accomplished, music is made—brilliant beyond past records.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds the mandate and governs the realm, your virtue surpassing former kings; with merit complete you now establish music, outshining all precedent.

sentences.zh: 臣聞五帝不相沿樂，三王不相襲禮，此蓋隨時改制，而不失雅正者也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the Five Emperors did not continue one another's music, the Three Kings did not inherit one another's rites—this is roughly reforming institutions as the age requires without losing elegance and rectitude."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Five Emperors did not inherit one another's music and the Three Kings did not copy one another's rites—each age reforms while preserving what is right."

sentences.zh: 」上竟從之，即改七懸八，以黃鐘為宮。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end followed this, at once changing the seven suspension to eight and taking Yellow Bell as keynote.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this, changed the seven-tone suspension to eight, and made Yellow Bell the keynote.

sentences.zh: 詔賁與儀同楊慶和刪定周、齊音律。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ben together with attendant of the first rank Yang Qinghe to revise and fix the pitch standards of Zhou and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Ben and Yang Qinghe, an attendant of the first rank, were ordered to revise the pitch systems of Zhou and Qi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜郢州刺史，尋轉虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed governor of Ying prefecture, soon transferred to governor of Guo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made governor of Ying prefecture, then of Guo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後遷懷州刺史，決沁水東注，名曰利民渠，又派入溫縣，名曰溫潤渠，以溉舄鹵，民賴其利。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to governor of Huai prefecture, cut the Qin River to flow east, named it the Benefit-the-People Canal, and also sent a branch into Wen county, named the Wen Moistening Canal, to irrigate saline fields—the people relied on its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Huai he diverted the Qin River eastward in the Benefit-the-People Canal and a branch into Wen county as the Wen Moistening Canal, reclaiming salty fields—the people prospered from it.

sentences.zh: 後數年，轉齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to governor of Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he was transferred to governor of Qi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 民饑，谷米踴貴，閉人糶而自糶之。

translations.literal: The people were famished; grain and millet leaped in price; he barred others from selling grain while selling it himself.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine, when grain prices soared, he forbade others to sell grain while selling his own stores.

sentences.zh: 坐是除名為民。

translations.literal: For this he was struck from the registers and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was struck from the rolls and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 後從幸洛陽，上從容謂賁曰：「我始為大司馬時，卿以布腹心於我。

translations.literal: Later, following on an imperial visit to Luoyang, the emperor said at ease to Ben, "When I first was Grand Minister of Martial Affairs, you laid bare your inmost heart to me.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on a visit to Luoyang, the emperor said to Ben at leisure, "When I first became Grand Minister of Martial Affairs, you opened your heart to me.

sentences.zh: 及總百揆，頻繁左右，與卿足為恩舊。

translations.literal: When I oversaw all affairs, you were constantly at my side—we are fully old friends in grace.
translations.idiomatic: When I took charge of all affairs you were constantly at my side—we are old friends indeed.

sentences.zh: 卿若無過者，位與高熲齊。

translations.literal: If you, sir, had no faults, your rank would be equal to Gao Jiong's.
translations.idiomatic: Had you been without fault, your rank would equal Gao Jiong's.

sentences.zh: 坐與凶人交構，由是廢黜。

translations.literal: Because you associated and plotted with evil men, you were for this dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: You plotted with wicked men and were cast aside for it.

sentences.zh: 言念疇昔之恩，複當牧伯之位，何乃不思報效，以至於此！

translations.literal: Speaking and recalling grace of former days, again given a regional lord's post—why do you not think to repay service and reach this point!
translations.idiomatic: Remembering our old friendship, I restored you to a governor's post—why do you not repay me and instead come to this!

sentences.zh: 吾不忍殺卿，是屈法申私耳。

translations.literal: I could not bear to kill you, sir—this is bending the law to declare private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I spared your life before—that was bending the law for friendship's sake.

sentences.zh: 」賁俯伏陳謝，詔複本官。

translations.literal: Ben prostrated himself and declared his apology; an edict restored his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Ben kowtowed in apology; an edict restored his former office.

sentences.zh: 後數日，對詔失旨，又自敘功績，有怨言。

translations.literal: Several days later, in responding to an edict he missed the intent, and again narrated his own merit with resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he answered an edict inappropriately, recounted his own merits, and spoke with resentment.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，顧謂群臣曰：「吾將與賁一州，觀此不可複用。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, turned and said to the assembled ministers, "I was about to give Ben a prefecture—seeing this, he cannot be used again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and told the court, "I meant to give Ben a prefecture—but after this he cannot be used again."

sentences.zh: 」後皇太子為其言曰：「此輩並有佐命之功，雖性行輕險，誠不可棄。

translations.literal: Later the crown prince spoke for him, saying, "These men all have the merit of assisting the mandate; though their nature and conduct are frivolous and dangerous, they truly cannot be cast away."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince pleaded for him, saying, "These men all helped establish the dynasty; though frivolous, they should not be abandoned."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「我抑屈之，全其命也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I have suppressed and bent them down—that is preserving their lives."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have kept them down only to spare their lives."

sentences.zh: 微劉昉、鄭譯及賁、柳裘、皇甫績等，則我不至此。

translations.literal: Without Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, and Ben, Liu Qiu, Huangfu Ji, and the rest, I would not have reached here.
translations.idiomatic: Without Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, Ben, Liu Qiu, Huangfu Ji, and the others, I would not be where I am.

sentences.zh: 然此等皆反覆子也。

translations.literal: Yet these sorts are all men of reversal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they are all men who turn with every wind.

sentences.zh: 當周宣帝時，以無賴得幸，及帝大漸，顏之儀等請以宗王輔政，此輩行詐，顧命於我。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan of Zhou, through rascality they won favor; when the emperor grew critically ill, Yan Zhiyi and others asked that a clan prince assist in government—these men practiced deceit and entrusted the charge to me.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan of Zhou they won favor through flattery; when the emperor was dying, Yan Zhiyi and others wanted a royal prince as regent, but these men tricked their way into entrusting power to me.

sentences.zh: 我將為治，又欲亂之。

translations.literal: I was about to bring order, yet they again wished to bring disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Just as I sought to govern, they wished to sow disorder again.

sentences.zh: 故昉謀大逆於前，譯為巫蠱於後。

translations.literal: Therefore Fang plotted great treason in front, Yi practiced witchcraft and curse-magic behind.
translations.idiomatic: Fang plotted treason; Yi practiced sorcery.

sentences.zh: 如賁之徒，皆不滿志。

translations.literal: Men like Ben and his sort were all dissatisfied in will.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Ben were none of them content.

sentences.zh: 任之則不遜，致之則怨，自難信也，非我棄之。

translations.literal: Employ them and they are not submissive; bring them near and they resent—it is hard to trust them of themselves; it is not that I cast them away.
translations.idiomatic: Employ them and they grow insolent; dismiss them and they nurse grievances—they are inherently untrustworthy; I did not cast them away lightly.

sentences.zh: 眾人見此，或有竊議，謂我薄于功臣，斯不然矣。

translations.literal: The multitude seeing this perhaps privately discuss, saying I am thin toward meritorious ministers—that is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Some may whisper that I have been harsh toward my founding ministers—that is not so.

sentences.zh: 」蘇威進曰：「漢光武欲全功臣，皆以列侯奉朝請。

translations.literal: Su Wei advanced and said, "Emperor Guangwu of Han wished to preserve meritorious ministers whole—all were made marquises attending court audience."
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei added, "Emperor Guangwu of Han wished to preserve his founding ministers by making them marquises who attended court."

sentences.zh: 至尊仁育，複用此道以安之。

translations.literal: Your Supreme Majesty nurtures with benevolence—you may again use this Way to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty in his benevolence may use the same method to settle them.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "So."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 」遂廢於家，是歲卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: He was thereupon retired at home; that year he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Ben was retired to his home and died that year at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 【史評】史臣曰：高祖肇基王業，昉、譯實啟其謀，當軸執鈞，物無異論。

translations.literal: [Historian's Comment] The historiographer says: When the Founder laid the foundation of the royal enterprise, Fang and Yi truly opened its stratagem; holding the axis and grasping the balance, things had no differing opinion.
translations.idiomatic: [Historian's Comment] The historiographer writes: When Emperor Gaozu founded the dynasty, Liu Fang and Zheng Yi opened the way; at the center of power, none disputed their standing.

sentences.zh: 不能忘身急病，以義斷恩，方乃慮難求全，偷安懷祿。

translations.literal: They could not forget their persons and hurry to the state's illness, break grace with righteousness; only then did they consider difficulty and seek completeness, steal peace and cherish salary.
translations.idiomatic: They could not forget themselves for the state's urgent need or sever private ties for public duty; they sought only their own safety and clung to their stipends.

sentences.zh: 暨夫帝遷明德，義非簡在，鹽梅之寄，自有攸歸。

translations.literal: When the emperor moved to bright virtue, it was not by simple selection in meaning; the charge of salt and plum had its own place to return.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor turned to worthier men, the role of chief minister naturally passed elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 言追昔款，內懷觖望，恥居吳、耿之末，羞與絳、灌為伍。

translations.literal: In speech they pursued former cordiality, yet within harbored divided hopes; they were ashamed to stand after Wu and Geng, disgraced to rank with Jiang and Guan.
translations.idiomatic: They spoke of old friendship yet nursed resentment within, shamed to rank below men like Wu Han and Geng, unwilling to stand with mere enfeoffed lords like Zhou Bo and Guan Ying.

sentences.zh: 事君盡禮，既闕於宿心，不愛其親，遽彰於物議。

translations.literal: Serving the ruler with full rites—they already lacked this in their long-standing hearts; not cherishing their kin, it was suddenly manifest in public discussion.
translations.idiomatic: They failed the loyalty they once professed and, by neglecting their parents, drew public censure.

sentences.zh: 其在周也，靡忠貞之節，其奉隋也，愧竭命之誠。

translations.literal: In Zhou they had no steadfast loyalty; in serving Sui they were shamed in the sincerity of exhausting their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou they showed no steadfast loyalty; under Sui they fell short of wholehearted service.

sentences.zh: 非義掩其前功，畜怨興其後釁，而望不陷刑辟，保貴全生，難矣。

translations.literal: Unrighteous conduct covered their former merit; stored resentment raised their later quarrels—and to hope not to fall under penal law, preserve nobility and keep life whole, was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Their later misconduct overshadowed their early merit, and the grievances they stored led to rebellion—yet they hoped to escape punishment and die in honor; that was vain.

sentences.zh: 柳裘、皇甫績、盧賁，因人成事，協規不二，大運光啟，莫參樞要。

translations.literal: Liu Qiu, Huangfu Ji, and Lu Ben accomplished affairs through others' strength, joined in plan without division—when the great fortune dawned in glory, they did not take part in the pivots of power.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu, Huangfu Ji, and Lu Ben rode others' efforts to success and stood together without wavering, yet when the dynasty was founded they were not admitted to the inner councils of power.

sentences.zh: 斯固在人欲其悅己，在我欲其罵人，理自然也。

translations.literal: This is solidly so: others wish them to please themselves; I wish them to scold others—reason is naturally thus.
translations.idiomatic: It is natural that they wished to please themselves while the emperor wished them to serve the state.

sentences.zh: 晏嬰有言：「一心可以事百君，百心不可以事一君。

translations.literal: Yan Ying had a saying: "One heart can serve a hundred rulers; a hundred hearts cannot serve one ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying said, "One heart may serve a hundred rulers, but a hundred hearts cannot serve one ruler."

sentences.zh: 」於昉、譯見之矣。

translations.literal: In Fang and Yi this is seen.
translations.idiomatic: This is plainly seen in Liu Fang and Zheng Yi.
